title: test-0093-SOC-ECO-PALAMPUR
passage: In the village of Rampur, the total land area available for cultivation has remained stagnant at 200 hectares since 1960. Farmers cannot expand this area further as all cultivable land is already in use, and clearing forests is strictly prohibited to maintain ecological balance. To boost output, farmers shifted from traditional seeds to High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds during the Green Revolution, which significantly increased crop yields per hectare rather than expanding the land size. For their daily operations, farmers must purchase inputs like chemical fertilizers and pesticides, which are classified as working capital because these items are consumed during the production process. In contrast, tractors and threshers are considered fixed capital as they are used over many years. The village productivity is not merely a result of the number of laborers, but depends on human capital, which refers to the education, skills, and health of the workforce. By investing in better irrigation and modern machinery, the village has successfully transitioned from subsistence farming to a surplus-producing economy without needing additional land.
